blocks.text: The fastest way to improve your speed is to stop using the mouse. On Mac, the Command key replaces the Control key from Windows. Use ⌘ + S to save often. Use ⌘ + C and ⌘ + V for copying and pasting. To move by word, hold ⌥ and press the left or right arrow keys. To jump to the start or end of a line, use ⌘ plus the arrow keys.

Most modern legal platforms like Clio or MyCase now offer drive utilities that sync directly with Finder. This lets you open Word documents without navigating through web portals. Treat your local folder structure like a digital filing cabinet. Keep case files organized by year and client name to avoid searching through endless downloads.

You spend over 22 hours a week typing. This leads to fatigue and mistakes. Use the built-in dictation features on your Mac to draft routine correspondence or simple memos. Hold the fn key to start speaking. Speak clearly and use punctuation commands like "period" or "comma" to keep your text clean.
If you are stuck on a specific Word feature, hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where it is. Lazur will draw a circle around the menu item so you can find it instantly.
blocks.title: Finding features quickly

items: Manual spacing: Use paragraph styles instead of hitting the return key repeatedly.
Inconsistent fonts: Set your default font to a standard legal typeface like Times New Roman or Garamond.
Broken numbering: Use the built-in list tools rather than typing numbers manually.

blocks.text: Lazur acts as a bridge between your questions and your screen. When you need to know how to create a table of contents or insert a section break, you do not need to hunt through help menus. Just hold the shortcut and ask. Lazur explains the steps while you keep your hands on the keyboard.

Legal documents often require complex formatting. Learn to use section breaks to change page orientation for large exhibits. Use the citations tool to keep your bibliography accurate. These small habits prevent massive formatting headaches later in the drafting process.
